title: EPIC 5: Aquarium & Income Rework — Claimable Income
description:
PRD AQUA-01..AQUA-09. Current code auto-adds income to cash every tick. PRD AQUA-05 requires 'claim accumulated aquarium income through a visible interaction or UI button.' This is a significant behavior change: income accrues to UnclaimedIncome pool, player must claim it.

PRD income model: 'Each stored fish has a fixed income-per-minute value. Server calculates earned income from elapsed server time and stored fish, then caps unclaimed earnings.'

title: TASK 5.1: Accrue income to UnclaimedIncome pool (not auto-cash)
description:

UX IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: Claim button must be impossible to miss. When UnclaimedIncome > 0, show pulsing/glowing indicator on HUD cash display + aquarium panel. Auto-claim on player leave (folded into save) so no income lost on disconnect. PRD says income accrues 'only while in-game' (AQUA-04) — UnclaimedIncome resets to 0 on load (don't persist it).

title: EPIC 1: Structured Data Model Foundation
description:

title: TASK 1.6: Bump DataStore key version for new profile format
description:
Current DataStore key is 'HarborHeist_PlayerData_v1' (DataManager.lua line 8). The new structured profile (1.1) is a breaking format change. Two options:
(a) Keep same key, rely on in-load migration (1.3) to upgrade — riskier (corrupts live     data irreversibly if migration bugs).
(b) New key 'HarborHeist_PlayerData_v2' with one-time copy+migrate from v1 — safer,     allows rollback, but loses v1 writes after cutover.

RECOMMENDATION: Option (b) for V1 closed test safety. Decide alongside DEC-1 since the income model affects what fields the v2 key must store.

WHY: Implied by migration work (1.3) but never explicit. Getting the DataStore key wrong risks permanent data loss for real players.

title: EPIC 3: Fishing System Rework — Timing Minigame
description:
Replace the current auto-catch (cast→wait→free fish) with a timing-based minigame and species-based catch resolution per PRD FISH-01..FISH-08.

Current FishingService: player casts, waits castTime seconds, gets a fish automatically. PRD FISH-03 requires 'a short, readable timing minigame' — a moving marker the player must stop in a target zone. PRD FISH-04: success awards fish, failure = retry-ready. PRD FISH-08: server determines result. FISH-02: bite-roll determined by zone+bait+rod+fish-table.

The minigame runs client-side for responsiveness (PRD perf table) but RESULT resolution is server-side. The server tells the client when a bite occurs; client runs the timing UI; client reports the timing result; server validates and resolves the actual species/value.
FILES: src/server/FishingService.lua, src/client/init.client.lua

Part of the Harbor Heist V1 build — migrating the current prototype to full PRD compliance (see PRD.md). The current codebase is a working server-authoritative prototype with 5 rarity tiers, basic cast/store/sell, passive income, and basic theft/lock PvP. title: TASK 8.5a: Raid target selection + eligibility validation
description:
PRD PVP-02, PVP-04, PVP-10 (partial). First half of the split raid flow.

Server-side raid target selection: given an attacker, enumerate eligible target docks (opted-in, not new-player-protected, not currently locked, not under immunity, not on per-victim cooldown). Validate the attacker's own eligibility (not on cooldown, raid window open). Return the eligible target list to the client raid UI (8.12).

WHY SPLIT: This is pure server validation logic that depends on the 'state' tasks (8.1 window, 8.2 opt-in, 8.3 protection, 8.4 lock). It can be built and tested as soon as those are done, WITHOUT needing the DEC-2 timing minigame design (which gates 8.5b). Decoupling target selection from outcome resolution cuts the critical-path depth and lets the raid UI show valid targets earlier.

title: TASK 8.5b: Raid timing minigame + outcome resolution
description:
PRD PVP-05, PVP-10 (partial). Second half of the split raid flow.

Given an attacker + validated target (from 8.5a), run the raid minigame and resolve the outcome per DEC-2 (hybrid timing) and DEC-3 (individual fish transfer). Server exclusively validates the timing input, rolls the theft outcome, and atomically transfers one eligible FishInstance. Applies loss caps (8.9), legendary protection (8.8), and triggers defender immunity (8.7) + notification (8.10).

WHY SPLIT: This is the actual skill gate + transaction logic. It depends on 8.5a (target already selected) and on DEC-2/DEC-3 (minigame model + transfer model). Everything downstream (8.6 cooldowns, 8.7 immunity, 8.9 caps, 8.10 notify, 8.12 UI, 10.4 atomicity) depends on THIS task, not 8.5a.

title: DEC-1: Passive income scope (online-only vs capped offline)
description:
PRD Open Decision #1. AQUA-04 says 'accrues only while in-game for V1' but the income model section implies elapsed-time calculation with a cap — tension.

RECOMMENDATION: V1 online-only accrual with a claimable income pool (don't auto-add to cash), capped to prevent extreme accumulation. Offline earnings deferred to V1.1.

UX RISK (important): Switching from auto-income to claimable income is a significant behavior change. Players used to cash ticking up passively may feel 'punished' if they forget to claim. Mitigation: make CLAIM button prominent, auto-claim on logout save, show a glowing '+$X ready to claim' indicator. If playtesting shows confusion, consider a hybrid: small auto-claim threshold + manual claim for the rest.

BLOCKS: Epic 5 income model + DataStore key versioning (1.6). PRD refs: AQUA-04, AQUA-05.
notes: DECISION: V1 online-only accrual + claimable pool. UnclaimedIncome accumulates while player is online, capped at MAX_UNCLAIMED. Player must CLAIM via button. Auto-claim on logout save. Does NOT persist on load (resets to 0). Offline earnings deferred to V1.1. Rationale: simplest exploit-resistant model that still creates the claim interaction the PRD wants (AQUA-05).

title: EPIC 10: Security & Anti-Exploit Hardening
description:
PRD security/anti-exploit section (lines 477-484). The current code already has good server-authoritative patterns (nil guards, bounds checks, capacity re-checks, distance validation). This epic formalizes it into an AntiExploitService + adds rate limiting, suspicious-action tracking, and audit logging.
